description: Sidecar metadata for continuous sampled signals (mouse trajectories, gaze, EEG). A small JSON document — named `<payload-filename>.timeseries.json`, stored beside its payload in the dataset's activity folder — declaring the payload's location, encoding, clock, sampling nature, and channels. Referenced from event streams via `attachments` (type `bdm:Timeseries`).

tables.name: TimeseriesMetadata
tables.description: The sidecar metadata document for one timeseries payload file.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Discriminator for the document kind; always `bdm:Timeseries`.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Short machine-friendly name of the series (e.g. `mouse_trajectory`, `gaze`, `eeg`).

fields.name: source
fields.description: Identifier of the physical device or stream that produced this series (e.g. `mouse0`, `eyetracker_left`). Matches the `bdm:source` carried by the run's recording events and by any discrete events from the same device — the join key stating which events and which timeseries describe the same device.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Human-readable description of what was recorded and how.

fields.name: content_url
fields.description: Where the payload file lives: a relative path resolved against this sidecar's own location (payload and sidecar normally sit side by side in the activity folder), or an absolute URL.

fields.name: content_type
fields.description: MIME type of the payload (e.g. `application/x-ndjson`, `text/csv`, `application/x-edf`, `application/vnd.apache.parquet`).

fields.name: content_encoding
fields.description: Optional transport encoding of the payload file, e.g. `gzip`. Absent means the payload is stored uncompressed.

fields.name: sha256
fields.description: SHA-256 hash of the payload file's bytes (after any content_encoding), lowercase hex. Recommended for integrity checking.

fields.name: byte_length
fields.description: Size of the payload file in bytes (after any content_encoding).

fields.name: clock
fields.description: URI of the clock every `t` value is on. Defaults to the vocabulary `engine_seconds` term: a monotonic per-session clock counting seconds since engine start.

fields.name: anchor_datetime
fields.description: The RFC 9557 datetime (with timezone offset) corresponding to `t` = 0 on the declared clock — the per-session bridge to wall-clock time. Optional here (the session-level record is the source of truth); duplicating it makes the sidecar standalone.

fields.name: sampling_nature
fields.description: Whether samples are event-driven (irregular) or taken at a nominal fixed rate.

values.description: A sample is written when something happens (e.g. the pointer moves); inter-sample intervals are irregular. The payload MUST contain a `t` channel.
Samples are taken at a nominal fixed rate (e.g. gaze at 120 Hz, EEG at 500 Hz). `nominal_rate_hz` is required; a `t` channel is optional (sample times are derivable from the index and rate).

fields.name: nominal_rate_hz
fields.description: Nominal sampling rate in Hz. Required when `sampling_nature` is `sampled`; meaningless (omit) when `event_driven`.

fields.name: runtime_id
fields.description: Identifies the activity run (one specific execution of an activity by one agent, distinguishing restarts) this series was recorded during. Resolves in the trial schema's `StudyflowLog` table and equals the event layer's `bdm:runtime_id`, so a sidecar can be tied to its run without relying on where the file sits.

fields.name: session_uuid
fields.description: UUID of the session this series was recorded in (see the trial schema's `session_uuid`). Lets a sidecar be interpreted standalone, outside the dataset folder hierarchy.

fields.name: attempt
fields.description: 1-based ordinal of the activity run within the session (see `attempt` in the trial schema's `StudyflowLog` table). Timeseries payloads keep a per-run filename because, unlike the tidy tables and the event stream, binary recordings cannot be concatenated into a single file.

fields.name: channels
fields.description: Definitions of the payload's channels, in payload column order. For self-describing payloads (e.g. EDF) this list mirrors the labels/units consumers need without parsing the container format.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Channel name as it appears in the payload (e.g. `t`, `x`, `y`, `Fp1`).

fields.name: datatype
fields.description: Datatype of the channel's values.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: Unit of the channel's values (e.g. `s`, `px`, `uV`). Omit for unitless channels.

fields.name: coordinate_frame
fields.description: For spatial channels: the coordinate frame the values are expressed in.

values.description: Pixels from the left/top screen edge (cf. the trial tables' x_screen/y_screen).
Fraction of screen width/height, 0 to 1 inclusive (cf. x_viewport/y_viewport).

fields.name: description
fields.description: Human-readable note about the channel.
